previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening dry heaves and abdominal pain following removal of her G-tube, with a history of gastric bypass and anastomotic ulcers. She was hydrated with IV fluids and started on IV proton pump inhibition. By hospital day 2, she tolerated a stage 4 bariatric diet. An upper endoscopy on day 3 revealed a small erosion in the gastric remnant cardia, with otherwise normal findings. She progressed to a stage 5 diet, remained stable, and was discharged home on oral pantoprazole and sucralfate with instructions for follow-up. Her symptoms improved with medical management, and no surgical intervention was required.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ presented to the hospital directly from clinic on 
___ due to persistent nausea, abdominal pain, dry 
heaves and inability to maintain adequate nutrition intake.  
Upon admission, intravenous fluids including a banana bag, 
intravenous pain/ nausea medication and pantoprazole were 
administered; nutrition labs were also obtained.  On HD2, a PICC 
was placed and TPN was initiated.  Nutrition was consulted and 
felt the patient was at risk for malnutrition.  TPN was 
gradually increased, monitoring closely for signs of refeeding 
syndrome of which there were none, to goal.  Once TPN reached 
goal, a nocturnal cycle was initiated and well tolerated in 
preparation for discharge.  

On HD5, the patient underwent an EGD, revealing mild gastritis 
and a small hiatal hernia.  Gastroenterology recommended 
increasing PPIs to 80 mg BID, which was implemented.  Also, 
cyclic vomiting syndrome was suggested as a cause for the 
patient's symptoms; the patient will follow-up with 
gastroenterology as an out-patient for further work-up.  
Following EGD, the patient was transitioned to all oral 
medication and the diet was advanced to stage 5 diet, which was 
well tolerated in small amounts. 

On HD6, the patient remained afebrile with stable vital signs.  
The patient's dry heaves and nausea had resolved and epigastric 
pain had improved.  She continued to tolerate small amounts of 
stage 5 diet; TPN was cycled nocturnally.  Additionally, she was 
voiding adequately and ambulating independently.  She was 
discharged to home on TPN with intravenous pantoprazole and will 
follow-up with gastroenterology and Dr. ___ on ___, respectively.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with nausea, epigastric pain, 
dry heaves and inability to consume adequate nutrition.  While 
hospitalized you were placed on TPN for nutritional repletion 
and intravenous pantoprazole, which will continue while at home. 
 Additionally, you underwent an EGD, which was revealing for 
mild gastritis and a small hiatal hernia.  Gastroenterology 
recommended increasing your pantoprazole, which was implemented 
at this time.  Your symptoms have gradually improved and you are 
now preparing for discharge to home with the following 
instructions:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.
Please resume all regular home medications , unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.
Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.
Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.
Incision Care:
*Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner if you have 
increased pain, swelling, redness, or drainage from the incision 
site.
*Avoid swimming and baths until your follow-up appointment.
*You may shower, and wash surgical incisions with a mild soap 
and warm water. Gently pat the area dry.
*If you have staples, they will be removed at your follow-up 
appointment.
*If you have steri-strips, they will fall off on their own. 
Please remove any remaining strips ___ days after surgery.
